bottleneck: A true memory prosthesis would need to replicate the hippocampus's encoding — transforming experience into durable, retrievable memory traces — but how the hippocampus writes memories is not understood at the algorithmic level. Stimulation studies can modestly boost recall in trials, yet no device can implant a specific memory or restore encoding in amnesia. We cannot build what we cannot specify, and the encoding algorithm may depend on distributed interactions no single device can replicate.
current_state: Hippocampal stimulation shows memory enhancement in small studies, but prosthetic memory restoration remains conceptual. The gap between boosting recall and replacing encoding is vast.

sources.title: Brain Connectome: Mapping Neural Networks in Neuroscience

title: Hippocampal memory encoding algorithm unknown
why_it_blocks: Memory loss defines Alzheimer's and devastates millions, yet the encoding algorithm is a black box. Without it, memory prostheses are impossible in principle, not just in practice — the blueprint itself is missing.
